_source: Published vendor specifications: dense (non-sparse) bf16 tensor-core peak and peak HBM bandwidth. These are SPEC-SHEET CONSTANTS, not fitted parameters, and not measured on our hardware. Keyed by canonical_device_key(), the same key the tuned tile artifacts use, so an unknown device fails CLOSED rather than falling back to a heuristic.
_cross_check: A100: 108 SM x 1.41 GHz x 2048 bf16 FLOP/SM/cycle = 312 TFLOP/s; 1512 MHz x 2 x 5120 bit / 8 = 1935 GB/s.
_omitted_on_purpose: Quadro RTX 8000 (Turing) is ABSENT twice over: it has no bf16 tensor cores at all, so a bf16 peak for it would be a fiction; and the owner's standing rule is that box is feasibility-only and never performance evidence. Failing closed there is correct -- an entry would invite someone to derive a band and report a number from it.
_source_h100: nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/h100 specifications table (read 2026-09-12): FP16 Tensor Core '1,979 teraFLOPS' (SXM) and '1,671 teraFLOPS' (NVL) are WITH sparsity; the dense peaks below are half of those. Memory bandwidth '3.35TB/s' (SXM, 80 GB HBM3) and '3.9TB/s' (NVL, 94 GB). Keys are what canonical_device_key() yields for the CUDA names 'NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3' and 'NVIDIA H100 NVL'. H100 PCIe is OMITTED until its datasheet figures are read at rent time (its bandwidth, 2 TB/s class, differs enough from SXM that a merged entry would misplace the ridge).
_source_rtx_5880_ada: nvidia.com RTX 5880 Ada datasheet (read 2026-09-16): 48 GB GDDR6, memory bandwidth 960 GB/s; 'Tensor performance 554.2 TFLOPS' is the sparse FP16-accumulate figure -> dense with FP32 accumulate = 554.2/4 = 138.6 TFLOPS (Ada halves tensor throughput under FP32 accumulation; SGLang GEMMs accumulate in FP32). Key = canonical_device_key('NVIDIA RTX 5880 Ada Generation').
_source_a100_40gb: nvidia.com A100 datasheet: A100 40GB SXM4 memory bandwidth 1,555 GB/s (80GB SXM4: 2,039; 80GB PCIe: 1,935); same 312 TFLOPS bf16 dense. canonical_device_key() strips the capacity token, so regime_switch_config() appends _40GB when the device reports < 60 GB (2026-09-16, CloudLab A100-40 row) so the 40 GB part gets its own band instead of the PCIe entry's.
